co_jungle_wall.blurb: Jungle Wall is a small sport crag in the Ptarmigan Creek cluster on the Aspen side of Independence Pass. It holds eleven climbs, nine of them bolted and two on gear, running from 5.8 up to the low 5.12s, with the bulk landing in the 5.10 to 5.11 range. The rock is blocky and edgy and often steep, and the routes are short enough that a 60 m rope is plenty. The setting is wooded: lines are strung out along the base and some stay hidden among trees until you are close. It is a steep uphill hike of roughly half an hour, so it suits a mid-grade sport day rather than a quick stop.
co_jungle_wall.approach: Short cairned path leaves the road shortly past the pullout; it climbs past two lower cliffs and then continues left and steeply uphill to the wall, about 30 minutes in total.

co_chicken_wall.blurb: Chicken Wall is the left-hand section of the Clock Tower crag in the Sport Park of Boulder Canyon, west of Boulder at around 8,000 ft. It has eleven climbs, mostly bolted with a few on gear, from 5.8 to 5.11. Most of them sit around 5.9 to 5.11, so it works well for climbers stepping up through the 5.10s. The crag catches morning shade, which makes it a comfortable choice when the weather is hot. The harder, steeper lines are over on the Upper Wall to the right; this side is the friendlier warm-up end of the crag. It is one of the more popular walls at the Sport Park.

co_red_devil.blurb: Red Devil is a large flatiron in the Central Flatirons above Boulder, about 6,800 ft up and visible from the Mesa Trail thanks to its strikingly red east face. A broad overhang cuts across that face, with a chimney or trough above it. The eleven climbs mix easy trad lines, a few sport routes and a top rope, ranging from low fifth class to the 5.12 range, so beginners can find a scrambly line while stronger climbers have bolted options. The rock is mostly sound, but a section on the south side of the red patch is flaking, so treat loose pieces carefully. A small leaning flatironette, the Unicorn, rests against its north side.

co_devil_s_advocate.blurb: Devil's Advocate is a small flatiron in the South Flatirons near Boulder, between the Maiden and Fatiron to the south and the Shanahan crags to the north, just under the north end of the Flying Flatiron. Routes lie on its east, west and north sides, with bolted lines on the south face. The eleven climbs are mostly gear routes with a few sport lines, spanning easy fifth class through the low 5.13s, including some crack climbing in the 5.9 to 5.11 range. It is quiet and seldom visited, windier than neighbouring crags, and the lower belays can run cold in shade. Best used as one stop on a day touring several formations nearby.

co_jungle_the.blurb: The Jungle is a small crag at Devil's Head in the South Platte region, at roughly 9,200 ft. The climbs are almost all bolted, with a single gear route, and run from 5.6 up to 5.11, with the heaviest concentration at 5.10. Several lines here are multi-pitch, which sets it apart from the single-pitch faces around it. Devil's Head as a whole is fine-grained granite with roofs, edges and flakes, and its crags generally face south, west or east with views toward Pikes Peak. The Jungle is reached on foot from the tourist trail rather than from the road.
co_jungle_the.approach: Hike the fire-tower trail roughly 1.5 miles, fork left for the Zinn Overlook, and turn off south at the split-rail fence.

co_fly_caster_wall.blurb: Fly Caster Wall is a small riverside crag in The Narrows section of Poudre Canyon, west of Fort Collins, at about 6,300 ft. It sits directly across the river from the Eden parking area. All eleven routes are bolted and fall between 5.10 and 5.12, with most split between 5.11 and 5.12, so it is a place for people already comfortable on harder sport climbing. The base is a sandy beach, and the climbing leans to short, bouldery, overhanging moves. Reaching it means crossing the river, which can be impractical at high water and is easiest when the flow is low in winter.
co_fly_caster_wall.approach: Leave the car at the Eden pullout, cross the road, and find a spot to wade or cross the river, usually just downstream.

co_block_tower.blurb: Block Tower is a trad-only formation within Cathedral Spires, in the South Platte area, around 7,400 ft. It lies between Poe Buttress and Cynical Pinnacle. The eleven routes are all on gear and range from 5.7 up to the 5.12s, with a core at 5.10 and 5.11, and several run to multiple pitches. Cathedral Spires as a whole is known for cracks, chimneys, offwidths and slabs, often put up ground-up with bolts only where needed. Expect a long, uphill walk to reach the base, with occasional cairns and some bushwhacking, so it rewards a full day out.
co_block_tower.approach: Reach it from the pullouts below Cynical Pinnacle, then hike left at the base of that spire and up and left to the tower, following cairns and a little bushwhacking.
